hero.badge: Privacy-first — your browsing history never leaves your device
hero.sub: EchoFocus tracks your active tab on-device, scores your focus, and sends Gemini nothing but an anonymized daily summary — domain names and minutes. No URLs, no page titles, no history upload.
hero.note: Free, and it runs in Chrome as a Manifest V3 extension. It isn't on the Chrome Web Store yet, so download the latest release build from GitHub.

preview.aiText: Your longest unbroken stretch was 96 minutes on github.com before lunch — the strongest block this week. Breaks clustered in the hour right after it.

how.title: Three steps, and only one of them touches a server
how.step1Desc: The extension reads the active tab through Chrome's tabs API and writes domain-and-duration entries straight into chrome.storage.local. It pauses when your machine goes idle or locks. No page content, no network request.
how.step2Desc: Each day your entries collapse into one summary: minutes per category, a focus score, and your top domains. That summary — and nothing else — is what the AI receives.
how.step3Desc: The analysis comes back to the extension popup, and to this dashboard if you sign in, where daily and 7- or 30-day trends accumulate.

privacy.title: Privacy is the architecture here, not a policy page
privacy.desc: Other trackers upload your history and promise to behave. EchoFocus structurally cannot: raw entries are written to chrome.storage.local on your machine, and no code path ships them anywhere.
privacy.leaves1: The date and total minutes per category
privacy.leaves3: Up to 8 domain names with minutes
privacy.leaves4: The insight text written from that summary
privacy.payloadCaption: The exact payload an analysis request sends — nothing is elided here
privacy.permsDesc: The manifest asks for tabs, storage, alarms and idle — plus identity for optional sign-in and notifications for the optional daily summary. There is no host_permissions entry, so the extension can never read a single page.

features.title: Enough signal to change how you work
features.f1Desc: No timers to start or stop. Active-tab time is attributed per domain and pauses the moment you step away.
features.f2Desc: Gemini reads your anonymized summary and writes back a short, specific read on the day — your actual patterns, not generic advice.
features.f3Desc: One 0–100 number weighing productive time against breaks & browsing, so today compares against your own baseline rather than someone else's.
features.f4Desc: Disagree with where youtube.com landed? Reclassify any site with exact-domain, subdomain-wildcard or URL-path rules on top of 100+ sensible defaults.
features.f5Desc: Sign in to keep daily summaries across devices and watch 7- and 30-day trends build up.
features.f6Desc: Export everything as JSON, or wipe local and cloud data in one click, whenever you want.

rules.title: Site rules
rules.intro: Rules decide which category a site counts towards. Yours take priority over the 100-plus built-in defaults, so anything the extension gets wrong you can correct here.
rules.syncNote: Rules are stored on your account. The extension applies them on its next sync.
rules.empty: No rules yet. Add one to move a site out of the category it landed in by default.
rules.matchExactHint: Matches that one domain and nothing else — notion.so, for example.
rules.matchWildcardHint: Matches a domain and every subdomain under it. Start the pattern with *. — for example *.google.com
rules.matchPathHint: Matches any URL containing the text you enter, so a section of a site can differ from the rest — for example youtube.com/playlist
rules.errorSpaces: A site pattern can't contain spaces.
rules.errorWildcard: A domain-and-subdomains pattern has to start with *. — for example *.google.com
rules.errorPath: A URL path pattern needs a slash — for example youtube.com/playlist
rules.errorSlash: A domain pattern can't contain a slash. Switch the match type to URL path.
rules.errorDuplicate: You already have a rule with this pattern and match type.

privacy.coreCommitment: Your browsing history is your private data. EchoFocus uses a local-first architecture — all raw browsing data (URLs, page titles, time spent) is stored exclusively on your device and is never uploaded to any server.
privacy.intro: EchoFocus handles your data at two levels:
tableRows: Aggregates only, when you sign in
Analysis text only — no raw browsing data

section2Items.label: Productivity tracking:
section2Items.text: Browsing behavior is analyzed locally on your device to produce daily stats and a focus score.

section2Items.label: AI analysis:
section2Items.text: Anonymized daily summaries (domain names + durations, never URLs) are sent to the Google Gemini API to generate personalized suggestions.

section2Items.label: Cross-device sync:
section2Items.text: When you sign in, your preferences, site rules and daily aggregates sync through Supabase so the dashboard works on any device.

privacy.section3Intro: EchoFocus relies on the following third-party services, each governed by its own privacy policy:

section3Items.label: Supabase:
section3Items.text: User authentication, preferences, and storage of synced aggregates and AI analyses. Data is encrypted and stored on AWS servers.

section3Items.label: Google Gemini API:
section3Items.text: AI productivity analysis. Receives only anonymized aggregate data — no URLs and no personal identifiers.

section4Items: Raw browsing records: automatically deleted after the retention period you configure (default: 30 days)
Daily aggregate stats: kept locally for up to 365 days
AI analysis results: kept locally and in Supabase until you delete them
Account data: kept until you delete your account
section5Items: Export or delete all local data from the Privacy tab of the extension's options page
Export or delete all cloud data from the dashboard's Profile page
Pause or disable tracking entirely from the extension
Sign out and keep using every local feature — an account is never required for tracking
privacy.section6Body: Local data is protected by Chrome's extension security model — no website or other app can read it. Cloud data is transmitted over HTTPS and encrypted at rest, and row-level security ensures each user can only ever access their own rows.
privacy.section7Body: EchoFocus is not designed for children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from that age group.
privacy.section8Body: We may update this policy from time to time. Significant changes will be announced through the extension; continued use after notice constitutes acceptance.
privacy.section9Body: For any privacy question, reach out via GitHub Issues.

guide.title: Guide
guide.intro: How EchoFocus works, and where each control lives. Nothing here changes your data — it is a reference you can come back to.
guide.howBody: The extension watches which tab is in front and how long it stays there, then writes the domain and the duration straight into your browser's local storage. It pauses when your machine goes idle or locks, and resumes when you come back. Visits shorter than five seconds are discarded, and a visit that crosses midnight is split across both days.
guide.scoreTitle: How the focus score is calculated
guide.scoreBody: Productive time divided by productive plus breaks-and-browsing time, as a number from 0 to 100. Neutral time — search, mail, calendars — is left out entirely, so a day spent mostly in your inbox neither helps nor hurts the score.
guide.categoriesNote: Over 100 domains are categorized by default, and you can reclassify any site with your own rules.
guide.privacyBody: Every URL you visit, every page title, and every individual visit with its timestamps are written only to your browser's local storage. No code path uploads them.
guide.privacyLeavesTitle: What is sent for AI analysis
guide.privacyLeaves: A daily summary: the date, total minutes per category, your focus score, and up to eight domain names with their minutes. That is the entire payload.
guide.whereExtensionItems: Tracking on/off, notifications, local data export and deletion, plus the same rules and preferences for when you are signed out
guide.whereDashboardItems: Daily and 30-day trends, AI snapshots and weekly reviews, focus hours, site rules, daily goal, idle timeout, data retention, language, cloud data deletion
guide.whereSyncNote: Site rules, daily goal, idle timeout and data retention can be edited in either place. They are stored on your account, and on the extension's next sync the account's copy is the one that applies.
guide.whereNote: Local browsing data can only be reached by the extension — that is the privacy architecture, not an oversight. Open the extension's options from its toolbar icon.
guide.demoDay: A sample day, drawn as sound
guide.formulaReads: The score is simply the productive share of your scored time:
